title: How Docker Works in 60 Seconds 🐳 #shorts
description:
"It works on my machine" — Docker fixes that. A Dockerfile builds an image (a read-only, layered blueprint of your app and everything it needs). lines: It works on my machine. But not on yours.
Docker fixes that. Here's how, in under a minute.
Your app needs the right version of Python, the right libraries, and the right settings. Change one thing, and it breaks.
Docker packs your code and everything it needs into an image: a read-only blueprint, built in layers from a Dockerfile.
When you run an image, you get a container: an isolated, running copy of your app.
Unlike a virtual machine, containers share the host's kernel, so they start in seconds and stay lightweight.
Need more? Run ten containers from the same image, on your laptop, a server, or the cloud.
And you share images through a registry, like Docker Hub. Pull, run, done.
